study: zero-shot resolution invariance, checkpoint selection corrected (second of the two B2 materials gated behind the Neo-Hookean rerun)

training.note_on_early_stopped: ran the full 4000-epoch budget without triggering patience 15 -- unlike Neo-Hookean (stopped at 3500) the best checkpoint (epoch 3350) was close to the end, so whether a longer budget would have found a better one further out is not known, same open question raised for B1 in PROJECT_STATUS.md
training.wall_clock_caveat: this run resumed from epoch 1651/4000 after a container restart lost track of an earlier segment; the reported wall clock covers only epoch 1651 onward, not the true total training time

reading.headline: B2 x Mooney-Rivlin works, 0.0661 to 0.3246 across seven unseen meshes -- comparable to Neo-Hookean's 0.0711 to 0.2691 and to B1's range 0.0504-0.1064, confirming the fixed-selection recipe is not specific to Neo-Hookean.
reading.the_crossover: Mooney-Rivlin is BETTER than Neo-Hookean at all three coarse meshes ([13, 17, 25]) and WORSE at all three fine meshes ([37, 41, 49]) -- the two materials' errors cross over somewhere between N=29 and N=37. Training was at N=21 and 33 for both materials, so this is not explained by one material training closer to the fine end.
reading.the_spread_is_wider_than_neo_hookean's: Mooney-Rivlin's spread across the seven meshes is 4.91x, wider than Neo-Hookean's 3.78x, both far wider than B1's worst case 2.11x. B2's resolution invariance is real for both materials and weaker than B1's for both, and weakest yet for Mooney-Rivlin.
reading.what_this_does_not_establish: Arruda-Boyce, the third B2 case, has not been evaluated yet (training just started, epoch 200 of 4000 as this file is written). Whether the coarse/fine crossover and the widening spread are a B2 pattern or Mooney-Rivlin-specific is not known until it finishes.
